text: vectra computes edit distances directly C engine, OpenMP parallelization columns exceeding 1000 rows. Three distance algorithms available. levenshtein() counts insertions, deletions, substitutions. dl_dist() (Damerau-Levenshtein) additionally counts transpositions adjacent characters single edit, better captures common typos like “hte” “”. jaro_winkler() returns similarity score 0 1, 1 means identical. weights early-character matches heavily, making well-suited short strings like personal names. Compute three metrics reference string filter edit distance. Normalized variants levenshtein_norm() dl_dist_norm() divide raw distance length longer string, returning value 0 1. makes thresholds transferable across strings different lengths. Damerau-Levenshtein catches transposition errors pure Levenshtein scores two edits. “ue” / “re” swap “Qurecus” counts 2 edits Levenshtein (delete + insert) 1 Damerau-Levenshtein (transposition). full coverage distance algorithms, threshold tuning, blocking strategies, see vignette("string-ops").

text: resolve() propagate() scalar self-join functions designed hierarchical (parent-child) data stored single table. operate within batch matching foreign key column primary key column batch, means entire hierarchy must fit within one row group (data must collected first). functions particularly useful taxonomic backbones, organizational charts, bill--materials structures row parent_id pointing another row’s id. resolve(fk, pk, value) returns value column row pk == fk. single-level lookup, equivalent self left-join (fk, pk), without overhead materializing hash table. lookup O(n) per batch (linear scan), works well hierarchies million rows. Row 1 (Fagaceae) parent_id = NA, parent_name NA. Row 3 (Q. robur) parent_id = 2, matches id = 2 (Quercus), parent_name “Quercus”. propagate(parent_fk, pk, seed) walks tree upward row fills every node nearest non-NA ancestor value seed. Unlike resolve(), single-level lookup, propagate() traverses full ancestor chain finds row seed expression non-NA. denormalizes hierarchy single pass, otherwise require recursive CTE SQL repeated self-joins dplyr. seed expression assigns “Fagaceae” root (row parent) NA everywhere else. propagate() walks row’s ancestry finds “Fagaceae” fills . four rows now carry family name.
code: taxa <- data.frame(   id        = c(1L, 2L, 3L, 4L),   name      = c("Fagaceae", "Quercus", "Q. robur", "Q. petraea"),   parent_id = c(NA, 1L, 2L, 2L),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) ft <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") write_vtr(taxa, ft)  tbl(ft) |>   mutate(parent_name = resolve(parent_id, id, name)) |>   collect() #>   id       name parent_id parent_name #> 1  1   Fagaceae        NA        <NA> #> 2  2    Quercus         1    Fagaceae #> 3  3   Q. robur         2     Quercus #> 4  4 Q. petraea         2     Quercus tbl(ft) |>   mutate(family = propagate(     parent_id, id,     if_else(is.na(parent_id), name, NA_character_)   )) |>   collect() #>   id       name parent_id   family #> 1  1   Fagaceae        NA Fagaceae #> 2  2    Quercus         1 Fagaceae #> 3  3   Q. robur         2 Fagaceae #> 4  4 Q. petraea         2 Fagaceae

title: Getting Started with vectra
text: vectra reads writes several file formats beyond .vtr. backend produces vectra_node plugs verb pipeline, can filter(), mutate(), group_by(), summarise() CSV files, SQLite databases, Excel workbooks, GeoTIFF rasters using identical syntax. key advantage streaming: format conversion pipelines (e.g., CSV .vtr) process data batch--batch without loading entire file memory. tbl_csv() scans CSV file lazily. Column types (int64, double, bool, string) inferred first 1000 rows probing field numeric, boolean, date patterns. Gzip-compressed files (.csv.gz) detected automatically file extension decompressed fly. batch_size parameter controls many rows read per batch (default 65,536). tbl_sqlite() scans SQLite table. Column types derived CREATE TABLE schema. filtering aggregation happens vectra’s C engine, SQLite. tbl_xlsx() reads Excel sheet via openxlsx2 package (Suggests dependency, required backends). sheet read memory data.frame, converted vectra node. streaming operation (full sheet loaded), makes possible chain vectra verbs Excel data without writing intermediate files. sheet argument accepts name 1-based integer index. tbl_tiff() reads GeoTIFF rasters. pixel becomes row x, y, band1, band2, … columns. Coordinates pixel centers derived affine geotransform stored TIFF metadata. NoData values become NA. enables spatial queries like filter(band1 > 25, x >= xmin, x <= xmax) rasters large load matrices. Results can converted back raster terra::rast(df, type = "xyz"). corresponding write_tiff() function reconstructs grid x/y columns writes GeoTIFF optional DEFLATE compression. Streaming format conversion common pattern. entire pipeline runs batch--batch, converting 20 GB CSV file .vtr stays within hundred MB memory. Write functions (write_vtr(), write_csv(), write_sqlite(), write_tiff()) accept vectra_node inputs consume batches upstream pipeline, writing batch output format arrives. format-specific options, batch sizes, performance considerations, see vignette("formats").

title: Getting Started with vectra
text: Three functions support incremental workflows .vtr files without full rewrites. designed append-heavy pipelines new data arrives batches (daily sensor readings, transaction logs, biodiversity occurrence records) rewriting entire file update prohibitively slow. append_vtr() adds new rows additional row groups end existing file. schema new data must match existing file exactly: column names, types, order. Existing row groups untouched; function writes new row groups last existing one patches header update row group count. fully atomic: process interrupted writing row groups patching header, file may corrupted. write-workloads atomicity matters, use write_vtr() (writes temp file renames). delete_vtr() marks rows deleted writing tombstone sidecar file (<path>.del). .vtr file never modified. next tbl() call automatically excludes tombstoned rows. Tombstones cumulative across multiple delete_vtr() calls. diff_vtr() computes key-based logical diff two snapshots dataset. returns list $deleted (vector key values present old file new) $added (lazy vectra_node rows present new file old). set-level difference based key identity, binary file diff row-level comparison. Rows key changed values appear $deleted $added, makes possible detect updates intersecting two sets. implementation streams files: pass 1 builds hash set old file’s key column, pass 2 streams columns new file writes added rows temporary .vtr file. temporary file cleaned automatically returned node garbage-collected. Keys 1 2 deleted. Keys 6 7 added. Key 3 appears changed value (“c” “C”), shows deleted added. incremental ETL patterns large-data workflows, see vignette("large-data").
code: fa <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") write_vtr(mtcars[1:16, ], fa) append_vtr(mtcars[17:32, ], fa) tbl(fa) |> collect() |> nrow() #> [1] 32 delete_vtr(fa, c(0, 1, 2))  # 0-based row indices tbl(fa) |> collect() |> nrow() #> [1] 29 unlink(c(fa, paste0(fa, ".del"))) fd1 <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") fd2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") old <- data.frame(id = 1:5, val = letters[1:5],                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE) new <- data.frame(id = c(3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L),                   val = c("C", "d", "e", "f", "g"),                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE) write_vtr(old, fd1) write_vtr(new, fd2)  d <- diff_vtr(fd1, fd2, "id") d$deleted #> [1] 1 2 collect(d$added) #>   id val #> 1  6   f #> 2  7   g unlink(c(fd1, fd2))

text: Every vectra pipeline builds lazy execution plan tree nodes. explain() prints tree data moves, makes primary debugging tool understanding engine call collect(). output shows node types (ScanNode, FilterNode, ProjectNode, SortNode, GroupAggNode, WindowNode, JoinNode, etc.), parent-child relationships, output column schema level. Several things look plan: Streaming vs. materializing. FilterNode ProjectNode streaming: process one batch time constant memory. SortNode, GroupAggNode, WindowNode materializing: consume input producing output. plan streaming nodes scan use memory proportional one batch, regardless file size. Column pruning. ProjectNode appears select() mutate() used. lists columns pass . Columns listed never decoded disk scan node, saving /O decompression work. Predicate pushdown. hash index exists filter column, ScanNode consults .vtri index reading row groups. explain() shows index file path pushdown active. Zone-map pruning (based per-row-group min/max statistics) applies columns automatically, without explicit index. Combining mechanisms gives fastest possible scan: index identifies candidate row groups key hash, zone-map statistics narrow set. Node order. plan printed bottom-(leaf root). ScanNode always bottom. Reading plan bottom top traces path data takes pipeline: scan disk, filter rows, project columns, sort, limit. glimpse() provides quick preview column types sample values without collecting full result. reads enough data show one line per column.

title: Star Schemas and Lookup
text: Ecological analyses almost always involve multiple tables. Observations live one file, species traits another, site metadata third, climate variables fourth. natural instinct join everything single wide data.frame early , work flat table rest analysis. works small datasets. scale, creates problems. biodiversity monitoring program 50 million observations, 12,000 species carrying 40 trait columns, 3,000 sites 25 metadata fields, climate grid 19 bioclimatic variables produces flat table 80 columns per row. analyses use 5 10 columns. remaining 70+ columns burn memory, slow scans, make column names collide across tables (requiring .x .y suffixes propagate downstream code). new trait column added species reference, every script built flat table needs updating. Relational databases solved decades ago foreign keys normalized schemas. data stays separate tables; queries join demand, pulling columns query needs. vectra brings pattern file-based analytical workflows three functions: link(), vtr_schema(), lookup().

title: Star Schemas and Lookup
text: star schema organizes data around central fact table (primary dataset measurements events) linked multiple dimension tables (reference data enriches facts). fact table holds foreign keys point dimension. database terminology, fact table sits center dimensions radiate outward like points star. ecological data, mapping direct: dimension table unique key. fact table references keys stores measurements. answer “average count per habitat type?”, need exactly two columns site dimension (site_id habitat) one fact table (count). flat table loaded 25 site columns 40 trait columns memory reason.

title: Star Schemas and Lookup
text: build schema three tables: field observations tree species across monitoring sites, species reference taxonomic conservation data, site metadata table. link() describes dimension table connects fact table. first argument key column (column name shared fact dimension), second vectra_node pointing dimension file. vtr_schema() ties fact table dimension links together. link gets name becomes alias used lookup() calls. print output shows fact table’s column count dimension key. schema object lightweight. holds pointers underlying files, copies data.

title: Star Schemas and Lookup

title: Species Distribution Models
text: synthesize small two-layer climate raster Central Europe write GeoTIFF EPSG:4326 GeoKey. Layer band1 stands mean annual temperature band2 annual precipitation. Now sample raster set survey sites. tiff_extract_points() returns one row per point input coordinates one column per band. Points outside raster come back NA. standardize two predictors store prepared columns, draw presence/absence outcome . Standardizing data reaches model lets every streaming batch share transform, --core fit relies . generating coefficients known, fit can checked .
code: nx <- 80; ny <- 50 xmin <- 5; xmax <- 17; ymin <- 45; ymax <- 55 xres <- (xmax - xmin) / nx yres <- (ymax - ymin) / ny  g <- expand.grid(col = 0:(nx - 1), row = 0:(ny - 1)) g$x <- xmin + (g$col + 0.5) * xres          # pixel centres g$y <- ymax - (g$row + 0.5) * yres          # row 1 is the northern edge g$band1 <- 14 - 0.6 * (g$y - 50) + 0.2 * (g$x - 11) + rnorm(nrow(g), 0, 0.3) g$band2 <- 750 + 25 * (g$y - 50) - 8 * (g$x - 11) + rnorm(nrow(g), 0, 10)  tif <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif") write_tiff(g[, c("x", "y", "band1", "band2")], tif, crs = 4326L)  tiff_crs(tif) #> $epsg #> [1] 4326 #>  #> $citation #> [1] NA N <- 1500 sites <- data.frame(   x = runif(N, xmin + 0.3, xmax - 0.3),   y = runif(N, ymin + 0.3, ymax - 0.3) )  env <- tiff_extract_points(tif, sites) head(env) #>           x        y    band1    band2 #> 1 12.185552 51.38240 13.48465 767.0959 #> 2 16.404559 46.80544 16.52226 624.3277 #> 3  7.619038 51.65444 12.43874 817.2647 #> 4  5.534852 53.85685 10.44774 896.6918 #> 5  6.119896 47.56621 14.34668 730.9303 #> 6 11.790835 52.69071 12.26763 796.8652 occ <- data.frame(   bio1  = as.numeric(scale(env$band1)),   # standardized once, then stored   bio12 = as.numeric(scale(env$band2)) ) eta <- -0.2 + 1.3 * occ$bio1 - 0.9 * occ$bio12 occ$presence <- rbinom(N, 1, plogis(eta)) table(occ$presence) #>  #>   0   1  #> 790 710

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: String-heavy datasets common ecology. Species names arrive typos, observer notes contain free-text descriptions, site labels mix upper lower case ways break joins. Cleaning matching strings often slowest part analysis pipeline, wall-clock time number lines R code required. vectra handles string operations inside C engine, operating directly raw byte buffers rather going R’s internal CHARSXP string pool. write mutate(name_clean = tolower(trimws(species))), expression serialized execution plan evaluated C data flows pipeline. temporary R character vectors allocated, intermediate copies exist, global string cache R maintains every unique character value bypassed entirely. architecture two practical consequences. First, string operations scale linearly data size suffer R’s O(n log n) string interning overhead. Second, CPU-intensive operations (regex matching, edit-distance computation) can parallelized OpenMP C engine owns memory layout. datasets thousand rows, vectra automatically distributes regex grepl, levenshtein, dl_dist, jaro_winkler across available cores. vignette walks every string operation vectra supports, basic transformations regex pattern matching fuzzy joins. use ecological data throughout: species names realistic errors, site labels field surveys, observer notes need cleaning analysis. examples deliberately small outputs fit screen, every operation shown works identically datasets millions rows, streaming memory one row group time without materializing full result collect() called.

text: literal substring matching enough, vectra supports full POSIX regular expressions passing fixed = FALSE. C engine compiles regex pattern per batch using regcomp() applies across rows. batches 1000 rows, matching loop parallelized OpenMP, thread compiling copy regex thread safety. regex dialect POSIX Extended Regular Expressions (ERE), dialect used grep -E Unix systems. means character classes like [-Z], quantifiers +, *, ?, alternation |, grouping () work expected. Backreferences replacement strings (\\1, \\2) refer captured groups. Perl-specific extensions like lookaheads, lookbehinds, non-greedy quantifiers (*?) supported; deliberate constraint keeps regex engine simple predictable.

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: build dataset species names various formatting issues. regex ^[-Z][-z]+ [-z]+$ matches properly formatted binomial names (capital genus, lowercase epithet, single space). Suppose want reformat species names “Genus epithet” “G. epithet” compact display labels. pattern captures first letter genus group \\1 entire epithet group \\2. Rows match pattern returned unchanged, consistent base R’s gsub behaviour.
code: tbl(f4) |>   mutate(short_name = gsub("^([A-Za-z])[a-z]+ ([a-z]+)$",                            "\\1. \\2",                            name, fixed = FALSE)) |>   select(name, short_name) |>   collect() #>                name        short_name #> 1     Quercus robur          Q. robur #> 2   fagus sylvatica      f. sylvatica #> 3  ACER PLATANOIDES  ACER PLATANOIDES #> 4    Betula pendula        B. pendula #> 5 Pinus  sylvestris Pinus  sylvestris #> 6     Tilia cordata        T. cordata

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: Exact string matching breaks data comes multiple sources inconsistent spelling. field botanist writes “Qurecus robur” (transposed letters), database export “Fagus silvatica” (single-letter substitution), citizen-science platform records “quercus ROBUR” (case mismatch). Fuzzy string matching quantifies different two strings lets us match records close enough. vectra provides three families distance functions, usable inside mutate() filter(). takes two string arguments (columns literals) returns numeric distance similarity score. raw variants (levenshtein, dl_dist) return integer edit counts; normalized variants (levenshtein_norm, dl_dist_norm) divide length longer string produce value 0 1; jaro_winkler returns similarity score 1 means identical.

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: levenshtein(x, y) counts minimum number single-character edits (insertions, deletions, substitutions) needed transform x y. result non-negative integer. levenshtein_norm(x, y) divides length longer string, producing value 0 (identical) 1 (completely different). “Qurecus robur” vs “Quercus robur” Levenshtein distance 2 (transposed “re” “er” counts two operations: delete insert, two substitutions depending alignment). “Betula pendula” matches exactly, giving distance 0.
code: typos <- data.frame(   field_name = c("Qurecus robur", "Fagus silvatica",                  "Acer platanodes", "Betula pendula",                  "Pinus sylvestrs"),   ref_name   = c("Quercus robur", "Fagus sylvatica",                  "Acer platanoides", "Betula pendula",                  "Pinus sylvestris"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) f7 <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") write_vtr(typos, f7)  tbl(f7) |>   mutate(lev = levenshtein(field_name, ref_name),          lev_norm = levenshtein_norm(field_name, ref_name)) |>   collect() #>        field_name         ref_name lev   lev_norm #> 1   Qurecus robur    Quercus robur   2 0.15384615 #> 2 Fagus silvatica  Fagus sylvatica   1 0.06666667 #> 3 Acer platanodes Acer platanoides   1 0.06250000 #> 4  Betula pendula   Betula pendula   0 0.00000000 #> 5 Pinus sylvestrs Pinus sylvestris   1 0.06250000

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: dl_dist(x, y) extends Levenshtein counting transpositions two adjacent characters single edit operation. better reflects kinds errors humans make typing. dl_dist_norm(x, y) normalized variant. Compare first row: “Qurecus” vs “Quercus” transposition “r” “e”. Levenshtein counts 2 edits, Damerau-Levenshtein counts 1. human-typed data, DL distance usually better default transposition errors common.
code: tbl(f7) |>   mutate(dl = dl_dist(field_name, ref_name),          dl_norm = dl_dist_norm(field_name, ref_name)) |>   collect() #>        field_name         ref_name dl    dl_norm #> 1   Qurecus robur    Quercus robur  1 0.07692308 #> 2 Fagus silvatica  Fagus sylvatica  1 0.06666667 #> 3 Acer platanodes Acer platanoides  1 0.06250000 #> 4  Betula pendula   Betula pendula  0 0.00000000 #> 5 Pinus sylvestrs Pinus sylvestris  1 0.06250000

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: jaro_winkler(x, y) returns similarity score 0 1, 1 means strings identical. Unlike edit-distance functions, higher values indicate better matches. Jaro-Winkler gives extra weight matching prefixes, making particularly effective personal names short strings first characters usually correct. scores 0.9 examples errors small relative string length. Jaro-Winkler less informative long strings small differences (everything scores 0.95) excels distinguishing short strings like surnames.
code: tbl(f7) |>   mutate(jw = jaro_winkler(field_name, ref_name)) |>   collect() #>        field_name         ref_name        jw #> 1   Qurecus robur    Quercus robur 0.9794872 #> 2 Fagus silvatica  Fagus sylvatica 0.9447619 #> 3 Acer platanodes Acer platanoides 0.9875000 #> 4  Betula pendula   Betula pendula 1.0000000 #> 5 Pinus sylvestrs Pinus sylvestris 0.9875000

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: choice depends error profile data: Damerau-Levenshtein (dl_dist / dl_dist_norm): best general default. Handles insertions, deletions, substitutions, transpositions. Use species names, place names, free-text field typos primary error source. Levenshtein (levenshtein / levenshtein_norm): appropriate transpositions rare need compatibility systems use classical Levenshtein. scores slightly conservative (higher distance) DL transposed strings. Jaro-Winkler (jaro_winkler): best short strings (15 characters) personal names. prefix weighting helps first characters reliable errors tend occur later string. Less useful long species names single-character change barely moves score.

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: practice, often want flag records exceed distance threshold reference value. filter species entries within normalized DL distance 0.15 “Quercus robur”. entries close “Quercus robur” survive filter. “Fagus sylvatica” “Betula pendula” distant, “Quercis rubur” sits right boundary (whether passes depends exact normalized distance).
code: field_data <- data.frame(   species = c("Qurecus robur", "Quercus robor", "Fagus sylvatica",               "Quercus robur", "Quercis rubur", "Betula pendula"),   plot    = c("A1", "A2", "B1", "A3", "B2", "C1"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) f8 <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") write_vtr(field_data, f8)  tbl(f8) |>   mutate(dist = dl_dist_norm(species, "Quercus robur")) |>   filter(dist < 0.15) |>   collect() #>         species plot       dist #> 1 Qurecus robur   A1 0.07692308 #> 2 Quercus robor   A2 0.07692308 #> 3 Quercus robur   A3 0.00000000

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: matching multiple candidates, sorting distance gives us best matches first. exact match scores 1.0, candidates small typos rank next. pattern useful building shortlist probable matches review manually.
code: tbl(f8) |>   mutate(sim = jaro_winkler(species, "Quercus robur")) |>   arrange(desc(sim)) |>   collect() #>           species plot       sim #> 1   Quercus robur   A3 1.0000000 #> 2   Qurecus robur   A1 0.9794872 #> 3   Quercus robor   A2 0.9692308 #> 4   Quercis rubur   B2 0.9358974 #> 5 Fagus sylvatica   B1 0.4769231 #> 6  Betula pendula   C1 0.3644689

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: fuzzy_join(x, y, , method, max_dist) joins two vectra tables using approximate string matching. argument named character vector length 1 specifying columns compare. result includes columns sides plus fuzzy_dist column normalized distance match. messy field name finds closest match reference table. fuzzy_dist column shows far apart , useful flagging matches might need manual verification (say, anything 0.15).
code: ref <- data.frame(   canonical = c("Quercus robur", "Fagus sylvatica",                 "Acer platanoides", "Betula pendula",                 "Pinus sylvestris", "Tilia cordata"),   family    = c("Fagaceae", "Fagaceae", "Sapindaceae",                 "Betulaceae", "Pinaceae", "Malvaceae"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) f_ref <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") write_vtr(ref, f_ref)  messy <- data.frame(   field_species = c("Qurecus robur", "Fagus silvatica",                     "Acer platanodes", "Betla pendula",                     "Pinis sylvestris"),   count         = c(12L, 7L, 3L, 15L, 9L),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) f_messy <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") write_vtr(messy, f_messy)  fuzzy_join(   tbl(f_messy), tbl(f_ref),   by = c("field_species" = "canonical"),   method = "dl",   max_dist = 0.25 ) |> collect() #>      field_species count        canonical      family fuzzy_dist #> 1    Qurecus robur    12    Quercus robur    Fagaceae 0.07692308 #> 2  Fagus silvatica     7  Fagus sylvatica    Fagaceae 0.06666667 #> 3  Acer platanodes     3 Acer platanoides Sapindaceae 0.06250000 #> 4    Betla pendula    15   Betula pendula  Betulaceae 0.07142857 #> 5 Pinis sylvestris     9 Pinus sylvestris    Pinaceae 0.06250000

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: method parameter selects distance algorithm. three options "dl" (Damerau-Levenshtein, default), "levenshtein", "jw" (Jaro-Winkler). using "jw", max_dist interpreted maximum dissimilarity (.e., 1 - jaro_winkler_score), max_dist = 0.2 keeps matches Jaro-Winkler score 0.8 higher. Jaro-Winkler produces tighter match set penalizes differences prefix heavily.
code: fuzzy_join(   tbl(f_messy), tbl(f_ref),   by = c("field_species" = "canonical"),   method = "jw",   max_dist = 0.15 ) |> collect() #>      field_species count        canonical      family fuzzy_dist #> 1    Qurecus robur    12    Quercus robur    Fagaceae 0.02051282 #> 2  Fagus silvatica     7  Fagus sylvatica    Fagaceae 0.05523810 #> 3  Acer platanodes     3 Acer platanoides Sapindaceae 0.01250000 #> 4    Betla pendula    15   Betula pendula  Betulaceae 0.01666667 #> 5 Pinis sylvestris     9 Pinus sylvestris    Pinaceae 0.02916667

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: Without blocking, fuzzy_join compares every probe row every build row. large tables quadratic. block_by parameter specifies column exact-match blocking: pairs share blocking key compared. taxonomic context, natural blocking key genus. split genus sides block , “Qurecus robur” compared reference rows genus starts “Q” (precisely, blocking column matches exactly). blocking, probe row compared one reference row (one sharing genus) instead six. real datasets thousands reference species, reduces number distance computations orders magnitude.
code: ref_blocked <- data.frame(   genus     = c("Quercus", "Fagus", "Acer",                 "Betula", "Pinus", "Tilia"),   canonical = c("Quercus robur", "Fagus sylvatica",                 "Acer platanoides", "Betula pendula",                 "Pinus sylvestris", "Tilia cordata"),   family    = c("Fagaceae", "Fagaceae", "Sapindaceae",                 "Betulaceae", "Pinaceae", "Malvaceae"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) f_ref2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") write_vtr(ref_blocked, f_ref2)  messy_blocked <- data.frame(   genus_field   = c("Quercus", "Fagus", "Acer",                     "Betula", "Pinus"),   field_species = c("Qurecus robur", "Fagus silvatica",                     "Acer platanodes", "Betla pendula",                     "Pinis sylvestris"),   count         = c(12L, 7L, 3L, 15L, 9L),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) f_messy2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") write_vtr(messy_blocked, f_messy2)  fuzzy_join(   tbl(f_messy2), tbl(f_ref2),   by = c("field_species" = "canonical"),   method = "dl",   max_dist = 0.25,   block_by = c("genus_field" = "genus") ) |> collect() #>   genus_field    field_species count   genus        canonical      family #> 1     Quercus    Qurecus robur    12 Quercus    Quercus robur    Fagaceae #> 2       Fagus  Fagus silvatica     7   Fagus  Fagus sylvatica    Fagaceae #> 3        Acer  Acer platanodes     3    Acer Acer platanoides Sapindaceae #> 4      Betula    Betla pendula    15  Betula   Betula pendula  Betulaceae #> 5       Pinus Pinis sylvestris     9   Pinus Pinus sylvestris    Pinaceae #>   fuzzy_dist #> 1 0.07692308 #> 2 0.06666667 #> 3 0.06250000 #> 4 0.07142857 #> 5 0.06250000

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: n_threads parameter controls many OpenMP threads distance computations use. default 4, reasonable starting point. workstation many cores, increasing 8 16 can help large joins. laptop processes need CPU time, reducing 2 reasonable.
code: fuzzy_join(   tbl(f_messy), tbl(f_ref),   by = c("field_species" = "canonical"),   method = "dl",   max_dist = 0.25,   n_threads = 8L ) |> collect()

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: fuzzy_join() streaming operation: probe side flows pipeline build side materialized hash table internally. sometimes need look reference repeatedly different query sets, rebuilding hash table time wasteful. materialize() converts vectra node persistent -memory block. materialized, can probe block_lookup() (exact matching) block_fuzzy_lookup() (fuzzy matching) many times needed without re-reading source data.

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: block_lookup(block, column, keys) performs hash-based exact match string column. hash index built lazily first call cached subsequent calls. result includes query_idx column maps result row back input key vector (1-based). Queries match multiple rows block return matches.
code: blk <- tbl(f_ref) |>   select(canonical, family) |>   materialize()  block_lookup(blk, "canonical",              c("Quercus robur", "Betula pendula")) #>   query_idx      canonical     family #> 1         1  Quercus robur   Fagaceae #> 2         2 Betula pendula Betulaceae

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: Field data often inconsistent capitalization. ci = TRUE parameter performs case-insensitive matching without requiring separate lowercased column reference. queries match despite case mismatch. Internally, engine builds separate case-folded hash index first use caches alongside case-sensitive one.
code: block_lookup(blk, "canonical",              c("quercus robur", "BETULA PENDULA"),              ci = TRUE) #>   query_idx      canonical     family #> 1         1  Quercus robur   Fagaceae #> 2         2 Betula pendula Betulaceae

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: block_fuzzy_lookup() computes string distances query keys every row block (, blocking, rows sharing blocking key). interface mirrors fuzzy_join() operates materialized block. block_col block_keys arguments work together: first query (“Qurecus robur”) compared rows genus == "Quercus", second query rows genus == "Fagus". blocking logic fuzzy_join() applied materialized block can reused across multiple lookup calls without re-reading disk.
code: blk2 <- tbl(f_ref2) |>   select(genus, canonical, family) |>   materialize()  block_fuzzy_lookup(   blk2, "canonical",   keys = c("Qurecus robur", "Fagus silvatica"),   method = "dl",   max_dist = 0.2,   block_col = "genus",   block_keys = c("Quercus", "Fagus"),   n_threads = 2L ) #>   query_idx fuzzy_dist   genus       canonical   family #> 1         1 0.07692308 Quercus   Quercus robur Fagaceae #> 2         2 0.06666667   Fagus Fagus sylvatica Fagaceae

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: String operations vectra fall three performance tiers. Understanding tier operation belongs helps predict bottleneck pipeline.

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: toupper, tolower, trimws, nchar, substr, startsWith, endsWith, paste/paste0 operate raw bytes O(n) single-pass algorithms. cost negligible compared disk /O. modern SSD, reading 100 MB string column takes roughly 50 ms; applying tolower adds less 1 ms, practice operations contribute negligible overhead compared /O cost reading data disk.

what: Tier 2: pattern matching (depends on pattern complexity)
title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: grepl, gsub, sub, str_extract compile POSIX regex (set fixed-string scanner) apply every row. Fixed-string matching (fixed = TRUE) tier 1 territory. Regex matching cost depends pattern: simple alternation like ^(|B|C)$ nearly fast fixed, pattern nested quantifiers like (.+?)* can exponentially slow pathological inputs. batches larger 1000 rows, engine distributes matching loop across OpenMP threads per-thread regex compilation, doubling available cores roughly halves wall time. practical advice: use fixed = TRUE (omit parameter, since defaults TRUE) whenever pattern literal string. Reserve fixed = FALSE cases genuinely need regex features like character classes, alternations, capture groups.

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: levenshtein, dl_dist, jaro_winkler compute O(mn) dynamic programming alignment pair strings, m n string lengths. column-vs-column comparisons mutate(), O(rows  m * n). fuzzy joins without blocking, O(probe_rows * build_rows  m  n). Blocking reduces O(probe_rows * avg_partition_size * m * n), matters much. loose max_dist change number distance computations, increases number rows survive threshold, many--many fuzzy join can cause combinatorial explosion output rows. tables contain 10,000 rows generous threshold matches probe row 50 build rows, result 500,000 rows. Tightening max_dist adding block_by column two effective ways keep output manageable. three distance functions use OpenMP parallelization input exceeds 1000 rows. work distributed schedule(dynamic, 64), meaning threads grab 64-row chunks finish, balances load well string lengths vary.

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: String-producing expressions (everything outputs new string column) use two-pass strategy. first pass computes output length row without writing bytes. second pass allocates single contiguous buffer fills . avoids realloc--copy pattern R uses internally, can fragment memory cause O(n^2) behaviour long strings. paste() many arguments gsub complex replacements, two-pass approach keeps memory allocation linear.

what: Which distance metric for which use case
title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: taxonomic name matching, dl_dist_norm threshold 0.15-0.20 workhorse. catches transpositions (common typo type Latin binomials), single-letter substitutions, dropped characters. reference list large can block genus, false-positive rate 0.20 low enough automated matching manual review pass distances 0.10. matching personal names (observers, collectors, authors), jaro_winkler threshold 0.10-0.15 (remember, dissimilarity, 0.10 means similarity score 0.90 higher) better choice. Names short, prefix weighting Jaro-Winkler exploits fact people rarely mistype first letter name. free-text fields errors include missing words, reordered words, abbreviations, none character-level metrics work well. Consider preprocessing tolower, trimws, gsub normalize strings computing distances.

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: Start conservative (low max_dist) increase gradually. max_dist 0.10 DL distance catches single-character typos strings 10+ characters. 0.20, start matching strings differ two edits, increases recall also increases false positives. 0.30, match set usually contains much noise useful without manual filtering. Jaro-Winkler, scale inverted (higher score = better match). max_dist 0.10 (score >= 0.90) reasonable starting point. 0.05 (score >= 0.95), catch minor differences. useful workflow run fuzzy join generous threshold, sort results fuzzy_dist, examine matches near boundary. gives empirical sense true matches end false positives begin specific data.

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: vectra operates raw bytes assumes UTF-8 encoding. input data Latin-1 another encoding, convert UTF-8 writing .vtr format. R, iconv(x, = "latin1", = "UTF-8") handles . data UTF-8, string operations work correctly ASCII characters pass multi-byte sequences without corruption, though distance metrics count bytes rather Unicode code points multi-byte characters. byte-level behaviour practical implication distance computation: strings contain accented characters encoded multi-byte UTF-8 sequences (e.g., “u” + combining accent), edit distance “u” “ü” larger 1 engine sees multiple bytes changing, single character. Latin-alphabet ecological data (species names, place names), rarely problem accented characters uncommon standardized taxonomic databases. data include accented characters, consider normalizing ASCII computing distances (e.g., replacing “ü” “u” via gsub).

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: typical cleaning pipeline chains several string operations matching. pattern use repeatedly species name standardization. pipeline strips whitespace, lowercases everything, removes periods, collapses multiple spaces one. mutate() call creates streaming node, chaining costs extra memory. cleaning, strings ready exact fuzzy matching standardized reference.
code: raw_names <- data.frame(   species = c("  Quercus ROBUR ", "fagus sylvatica.",               "Acer platanoides (L.)", "BETULA   pendula"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) f9 <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") write_vtr(raw_names, f9)  tbl(f9) |>   mutate(clean = tolower(trimws(species))) |>   mutate(clean = gsub(".", "", clean, fixed = TRUE)) |>   mutate(clean = gsub(" +", " ", clean, fixed = FALSE)) |>   select(species, clean) |>   collect() #>                 species                clean #> 1        Quercus ROBUR         quercus robur #> 2      fagus sylvatica.      fagus sylvatica #> 3 Acer platanoides (L.) acer platanoides (l) #> 4      BETULA   pendula       betula pendula

title: String Operations and Fuzzy Matching
text: effective matching strategy layers exact fuzzy methods. Start exact join cleaned names (catching easy cases near-zero cost), run fuzzy join unmatched remainder. avoids spending CPU cycles distance computations records match perfectly basic cleaning. Records status NA match exactly go second pass fuzzy_join(). example four match cleaning, ideal outcome: fuzzy join handles genuinely ambiguous cases. layered strategy reflects taxonomic name resolution works practice. Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) backbone taxonomy, instance, contains 7 million names. Running fuzzy join full list every input record prohibitively expensive. Cleaning first, exact-matching second, fuzzy-matching remainder keeps computational cost proportional number genuinely problematic records rather total dataset size. typical citizen-science dataset, 80-90% records match exactly basic normalization, leaving 10-20% distance computation stage.
code: ref_clean <- data.frame(   canonical = c("quercus robur", "fagus sylvatica",                 "acer platanoides", "betula pendula"),   status    = c("accepted", "accepted", "accepted", "accepted"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) f_refc <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") write_vtr(ref_clean, f_refc)  cleaned <- tbl(f9) |>   mutate(clean = tolower(trimws(species))) |>   mutate(clean = gsub(".", "", clean, fixed = TRUE)) |>   mutate(clean = gsub(" +", " ", clean, fixed = FALSE))  # Step 1: exact join on cleaned names exact <- left_join(   cleaned, tbl(f_refc),   by = c("clean" = "canonical") ) |> collect()  exact #>                 species                clean   status #> 1        Quercus ROBUR         quercus robur accepted #> 2      fagus sylvatica.      fagus sylvatica accepted #> 3      BETULA   pendula       betula pendula accepted #> 4 Acer platanoides (L.) acer platanoides (l)     <NA>

text: optimizer rewrites plan data moves, execution streams result rather materializing : Streaming execution: one row group flows time, never whole file Column pruning: columns never reference skipped scan Predicate pushdown: per-rowgroup min/max statistics skip row groups match filter Hash joins: build right side, stream left; join fact table lookup without holding memory External sort: memory budget automatic spill disk explain() shows optimized plan, including columns row groups pruned:
code: tbl("data.vtr") |>   filter(x > 0) |>   select(id, x) |>   explain() #> vectra execution plan #> #> ProjectNode [streaming] #>   FilterNode [streaming] #>     ScanNode [streaming, 2/5 cols (pruned), predicate pushdown, v3 stats]

title: Columnar Query Engine for Larger-than-RAM Data

what: Streaming results into a model fit
title: Columnar Query Engine for Larger-than-RAM Data
text: collect() brings whole result memory. collect_chunked() folds function query one batch time, holding single batch plus accumulator, result larger memory reduces small summary one pass: running count, per-group sufficient statistics, cross-products behind linear fit. models re-read data every iteration, chunk_feeder() exposes query resettable generator biglm::bigglm() drives directly, fitting GLM data large hold memory: offload() spills prepared query disk streams back, reweighted pass reads prepared columns file rather rebuilding pipeline. key instead splits query per-key shards disk, turning model couples within group set independent per-shard fits. group_map() runs function shard returns results keyed shard; group_modify() recombines per-shard data.frames one table.
code: # Accumulate X'X and X'y for an exact OLS fit, one streaming batch at a time acc <- tbl("survey.vtr") |>   select(mpg, wt, hp) |>   collect_chunked(     function(acc, chunk) {       X <- cbind(1, chunk$wt, chunk$hp)       list(XtX = acc$XtX + crossprod(X),            Xty = acc$Xty + crossprod(X, chunk$mpg))     },     .init = list(XtX = matrix(0, 3, 3), Xty = matrix(0, 3, 1))   ) solve(acc$XtX, acc$Xty) src <- function() tbl("occurrences.vtr") |> select(presence, bio1, bio12) biglm::bigglm(presence ~ bio1 + bio12, data = chunk_feeder(src),               family = binomial()) # Prepare once, then let bigglm re-read the spill on every pass s <- offload(tbl("occurrences.vtr") |> select(presence, bio1, bio12)) biglm::bigglm(presence ~ bio1 + bio12, data = chunk_feeder(s),               family = binomial())  # Per-region fits: each shard fits in memory on its own p <- offload(tbl("occurrences.vtr"), by = "region") fits <- group_map(p, function(d, region)   glm(presence ~ bio1 + bio12, data = d, family = binomial()))

title: Turn a query into a resettable chunk generator — chunk_feeder
text: vectra node consumed streams, re-reading requires fresh node pass. chunk_feeder() accepts either form: factory, function arguments returns new node time called; offloaded node offload(), backed file replays disk directly. every reset = TRUE fresh stream started, query replayed pass. text: x vectra_node (tbl(), tbl_csv(), tbl_tiff(), ... chain verbs). consumed: collect_chunked() returns, stream drained x collected . f function two arguments function(acc, chunk) returning updated accumulator. chunk data.frame holding next batch rows. .init Initial accumulator value. Passed f first batch returned unchanged query yields rows. combine supplied also monoid identity (value combine leaves unchanged). combine Optional function function(acc, acc) merges two accumulators. Supplying declares reduction monoid .init identity, lets fold run independent shards partition (offload(x, = ...)) partial results merged correctly. plain node stream single sequence, combine needed ignored. commutative Logical; declare combine depend order arguments. text: streaming counterpart fold (Reduce()): use query returns rows fit memory reduction small. running count, per-group sufficient statistics, cross-products X'X X'y behind linear fit, online mean histogram - accumulate bounded space across stream. instead need model-fitting consumer drive iteration (re-read data pass, iteratively reweighted GLM ), use chunk_feeder().

title: Fold a function over a query, one batch at a time — collect_chunked
code: f <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") write_vtr(mtcars, f)  # Row count without materializing the result. collect_chunked(tbl(f), function(acc, chunk) acc + nrow(chunk), .init = 0L)  # Accumulate the normal-equation pieces X'X and X'y for an exact OLS fit # of mpg ~ wt + hp, in one streaming pass. acc <- collect_chunked(   tbl(f) |> select(mpg, wt, hp),   function(acc, chunk) {     X <- cbind(1, chunk$wt, chunk$hp)     y <- chunk$mpg     list(XtX = acc$XtX + crossprod(X), Xty = acc$Xty + crossprod(X, y))   },   .init = list(XtX = matrix(0, 3, 3), Xty = matrix(0, 3, 1)) ) solve(acc$XtX, acc$Xty)            # same as coef(lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, mtcars)) unlink(f)

code: # From a data.frame f <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") write_vtr(mtcars, f)  # Streaming format conversion (CSV -> VTR) csv <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv") write.csv(mtcars, csv, row.names = FALSE) f2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".vtr") tbl_csv(csv) |> write_vtr(f2)  unlink(c(f, f2, csv))

title: vectra 0.7.1
text: Cap OpenMP team two threads R CMD check. CRAN’s _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_ set, package now lowers default team size two parallel string, fuzzy-join, sort, window kernels stay within check farm’s two-core limit. fuzzy-join match phase also clamps requested thread count available maximum, matching blocked fuzzy-lookup path. Outside check package still uses every available core.

title: vectra 0.7.0
text: collect_chunked(x, f, .init) folds function query one batch time. engine pulls single batch R, applies f(acc, chunk), frees batch, moves , result larger RAM can reduced small summary (running count, per-group sufficient statistics, cross-products behind linear fit) one bounded-memory pass. chunk_feeder(.source) turns query resettable generator following data(reset) protocol biglm::bigglm() expects, generalized linear model can fitted --core: iteratively reweighted pass streams engine without ever holding full design matrix. .source factory returning fresh node, replayed every reset. New C pull interface (C_node_optimize, C_node_next_batch) backs verbs; per-batch conversion reuses existing column converter, chunked materializing paths share one code path.

title: vectra 0.7.0
text: offload() one verb two return shapes. offload(x) materializes query .vtr returns node streams file: holds rows x (identity values) changes cost profile, since replaying disk scan instead re-run upstream pipeline. chunk_feeder() accepts offloaded node directly, iterative consumer biglm::bigglm() reads prepared columns disk every reweighted pass rather rebuilding time. offload(x, = ...) splits query disjoint shards single streaming pass, one per key value (method = "level"), per value range ("range"), per hash bucket ("hash"); "auto" picks level discrete key range numeric one. result list-like: length(), names() (keys), p[["key"]], lapply(p, ...) work, turning model couples within group independent per-shard fits. union shards reproduces input; row totals checked. group_map() group_modify() run function shard partition. group_map() reads shard data.frame, hands function key, returns results keyed shard (one fit per group). group_modify() binds per-shard data.frames one table restores key column. purrr-style ~ formula works either. collect_chunked() now generic gains combine argument: supplying declares reduction monoid (.init identity), lets fold run shards partition merge partial results. commutative flag declares merge order-free. Offloaded streams carry cost grade (passes data, peak memory, /O class), shown print() explain() – label plan reads choose one-pass fold, external sort (arrange()), partition.

title: vectra 0.6.3
text: summarise() / summarize() now accept namespace-qualified aggregation calls (vectra::n(), vectra::sum(x), vectra:::mean(x)). Previously parse_agg_expr ran .character() call head dispatched result; pkg::fn call yielded length-3 vector c("::", "pkg", "fn"), subsequent (!fn %% valid_aggs) triggered “condition length > 1” R >= 4.2. parser now unwraps :: / ::: uses bare function name.

title: vectra 0.6.2
text: Resolves three findings auto-check email surfaced 2026-05-06 archived 0.5.1 release. DESCRIPTION: replaced “gridded” (flagged possibly-misspelled word CRAN incoming pretest) “raster”. gcc-ASAN heap-buffer-overflow LZ decode path (tdc/src/api/decode_impl.c, surfaced read_rg_tdc_with_fp vtr1_tdc.c): consolidated decode pipeline now always allocates scratch buffers +16-byte wildcopy slack, tdc_match_copy’s SIMD overshoot stays within allocation. decode_ex.c variant missing slack 0.5.1 gone (folded shared driver_decode_block_impl). ASAN--vignettes regression check now part GitHub Actions sanitizer workflow future drift caught locally instead CRAN’s BDR memcheck. rchk PROTECT findings src/r_bridge.c, src/r_bridge_io.c, src/vtr1_tdc.c, src/collect.c: every Rf_getAttrib / Rf_mkString result crossed allocating call (R_alloc, Rf_warning, Rf_setAttrib, Rf_asReal, Rf_asInteger, parse_*) now PROTECTed balanced matching UNPROTECT. Touches apply_annotation, C_write_vtr, C_write_vtr_tdc, parse_quantize, parse_spatial.

title: vectra 0.6.1
text: src/vec_omp.h call sites: stop including <omp.h> forward-declare three OpenMP runtime functions vectra calls (omp_get_max_threads, omp_get_thread_num, omp_in_parallel). clang 21’s bundled omp.h wrapper contains unbalanced #pragma omp end declare variant breaks compilation block.c (vectra TU includes wrapper) r-devel-linux-x86_64-debian-clang. bug wrapper , #ifdef _OPENMP guard around #include <omp.h> enough — -fopenmp compile line, _OPENMP defined broken wrapper pulled . Skipping wrapper avoids bug; #pragma omp ... directives elsewhere src/ still recognised runtime symbols resolve link time via libomp. Fixes compilation error caused vectra 0.5.1 archived CRAN.

title: vectra 0.6.0
text: new tiled raster format accompanying API larger--RAM gridded data. tile encoded self-describing tdc block (PRED_2D + BYTE_SHUFFLE + LZ); decoding parallel across tiles. vec_write_raster(x, path, ...): write numeric matrix 3D (rows, cols, bands) array .vec. Storage dtypes: f64, f32, i8/u8, i16/u16, i32/u32, i64/u64. compression controls per-tile codec probing — "fast", "balanced", "max" (six-spec probe per tile). Decode cost unchanged across levels tile records codec spec. vec_open_raster(path) / vec_close_raster(r): lazy open returning metadata + handle list (vectra_raster). handle auto-finalized garbage collection. vec_read_window(r, band, level, cols, rows): decode window chosen band, overview-level support. Pixels outside raster come back NA. Tile decode parallelized across worker threads (Phase 5a). vec_extract_points(r, x, y): sample band values (x, y) points. vec_build_overviews(path, levels, resampling): append n_levels - 1 reduced-resolution copies place. Resampling kernels: "nearest", "average", "bilinear", "mode", "gauss". file’s n_levels updated atomically. vec_to_tiff(path, output, compression): export .vec level-0 pixels GeoTIFF. Compression "none", "deflate", "lzw"; LZW also applies horizontal differencing (Predictor 2) integer pixel types, matching layout libtiff/GDAL produce default. Inherits dtype, geotransform, EPSG, nodata source.

title: vectra 0.6.0
text: "image" (default): one tile per (band, time, ty, tx) — optimal “give one full image time T” reads. "pixel": one tile per (band, ty, tx) holding full time stack [tw*th, n_time] — optimal “give time series pixel (x, y)” reads. vec_read_pixel_series(r, x, y, band): full time series single pixel numeric vector. pixel-major files one tile decode; image-major files reader scans index distinct time stamps decodes one tile per stamp. vec_read_time_slice(r, time, band, level, cols, rows): read single time slice matrix. vec_raster_times(r, band, level): distinct time stamps, ascending order. vec_raster_layout(r): query whether open raster "image" "pixel" layout. print.vectra_raster(): prints dimensions, dtype, geotransform, EPSG, nodata, band names.

title: vectra 0.6.0
text: Reader: tiled Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) inputs go block abstraction strip TIFFs (strips collapse n_blocks_x = 1). Edge-block padding handled block_stored_rows(). tiff_band_names(): parse <Item role="description"> entries GDAL_METADATA (tag 42112). Pure-R scanner, xml2 dependency. tiff_crs(path): read EPSG code, geographic-vs-projected flag, citation string GeoKey directory (tags 34735/34737). tiled = TRUE emits TIFF tags 322/323/324/325 place strip tags. tile_size accepts single integer (square) length-2 c(w, h); dimensions must positive multiples 16. Default 256. Tiled output layout required Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF. bigtiff = "auto" (default) auto-promotes BigTIFF (magic 0x002B, 64-bit offsets) expected raw payload exceeds classic-TIFF 4 GB ceiling; TRUE forces BigTIFF; FALSE forces classic TIFF. Tiled BigTIFF yet supported. crs accepts integer EPSG code, "EPSG:xxxx" string, list $epsg, $geographic, optional $citation. Outputs round-trip terra::rast() 4326, 3857, 31287.

title: vectra 0.6.0
text: collect() / block_array_gather: empty-string slots now shortcut R_BlankString. Previously gather paths called Rf_mkCharLenCE(NULL, 0, ...) dedup cache called memcmp(NULL, ...) batch happened contain empty/NA strings, tripping UBSAN’s nonnull check even though length zero.

title: vectra 0.6.0
text: C-side *_push helpers (vec_buf_push, vec_array_push, …) consolidated single vec_grow_to growth primitive.

title: vectra 0.5.1
text: configure / configure.win: rewritten POSIX /bin/sh (previously #!/usr/bin/env bash set -o pipefail [[ ... ]]). Bash guaranteed CRAN build hosts. src/window.c: OpenMP task-parallel merge sort helper defined unconditionally called #ifdef _OPENMP branches, producing clang -Wunneeded-internal-declaration warning Debian’s -OpenMP build. definition now shares guard. Vendored tdc: fprintf(stderr, ...) debug/timing prints routed TDC_LOG(...) macro -op unless TDC_ENABLE_STDERR_LOG defined build time, released .contains stderr / fprintf symbols. Addresses WRE §1.6.4 policy forbidding compiled code writing stdout/stderr.

title: vectra 0.5.1
text: collect(): fix use--free cross-batch CHARSXP dedup cache. slot stored raw pointer decoder’s heap buffer, freed batch consumed; next batch’s hash-collision memcmp dereferenced freed memory. Manifested segfaults second consecutive collect() large multi-rowgroup string-heavy .vtr (register, backbones), likely parallel reader batches accumulate serial consumer loop. Now verifies cache hits CHAR(sexp), points still-alive interned CHARSXP body.

title: vectra 0.5.0
text: Replaced bespoke v4 codec tdc, standalone typed-dimensional compression library vendored src/tdc/. Encode decode go self-describing block record (model + transform chain + entropy) rather per-column tag constants. Deleted vtr_codec.c, vtr_encodings.c, vtr_compress.c, vtr1.c, vtr_codec_internal.h. .vtr -disk format deliberate breaking change: pre-0.5 files readable. write_vtr() append_vtr() write new container; tbl() reads new container. Per-row-group column statistics (min/max) carried container index scan layer can still prune unreachable row groups. Parallel row-group reads preserved. Custom vendoring via tools/vendor_tdc.sh configure / configure.win pull latest upstream tdc every install source checkout present; pre-vendored copy used otherwise.

title: vectra 0.5.0
text: v4 dict-defer CHARSXP fast path gone — duplicate strings now hit R’s CHARSXP hash per row. re-implemented top tdc’s dictionary-encoded varlen output becomes hot spot.

title: vectra 0.5.0
text: man/write_vtr.Rd: replaced literal percent sign compress argument description produced malformed Rd output build. Windows: write_vtr(), append_vtr() delete_vtr() now use MoveFileEx short retry loop final temp--target swap. Previously, preceding tbl() read leave target file mmap’d pending GC, swap fail sharing violation.

title: vectra 0.4.1
text: New vtr_schema(), link(), lookup() functions star-schema workflows. Register fact table named dimension links , pull columns dimension without writing explicit joins. referenced dimensions scanned. lookup() reports unmatched keys per dimension default, catching referential integrity issues propagate NAs silently. Supports "left" (default) "inner" join modes, named keys differing column names, reusable schema objects across multiple queries.

title: vectra 0.3.2
text: Fix misaligned int64_t memory access vtr_codec.c (UBSAN). Dictionary encoding wrote read 8-byte offsets unaligned pointer; delta decoding issue. fixed memcpy.

title: vectra 0.3.1
text: CRAN submission fixes: title case, quoted technical terms DESCRIPTION, corrected documentation URLs.

title: vectra 0.3.0
text: append_vtr(df, path): append data.frame new row group existing .vtr file. Existing row groups never rewritten. delete_vtr(path, row_ids): logically delete rows 0-based physical index. Writes tombstone side file (<path>.del); .vtr file never modified. Deletions cumulative excluded automatically next tbl() call. diff_vtr(old_path, new_path, key_col): key-based logical diff two .vtr files. Returns list added (lazy vectra_node) deleted (vector key values). Implemented single-pass C streaming engine O(n_unique_keys) memory.

title: vectra 0.3.0
text: tolower(), toupper(), trimws(): case conversion whitespace trimming string columns filter() mutate(). levenshtein(x, y) / levenshtein_norm(x, y): Levenshtein edit distance normalised variant (0–1). Supports column-vs-column column-vs-literal comparisons. Optional max_dist argument early termination. dl_dist(x, y) / dl_dist_norm(x, y): Damerau-Levenshtein distance (counts transpositions cost 1) normalised variant. jaro_winkler(x, y): Jaro-Winkler similarity (0–1, higher = similar). string-similarity functions propagate NA work filter() mutate(). resolve(fk, pk, value): scalar self-join — looks value pk == fk within batch. Useful denormalising parent-child tables without join. propagate(parent_id, id, seed): tree-traversal aggregation — propagates non-NA seed values parent-child hierarchy reachable nodes filled. Converges O(depth) passes.

title: vectra 0.3.0
text: Encoding: PLAIN (default), DICTIONARY (string columns < 50% unique values), DELTA (monotonically increasing int64 columns). Compression: custom LZ77 byte compressor (LZ_VTR, ~120 lines C). Applied encoding; skipped buffers < 64 bytes compression reduce size. Files written v4 typically 30–60% smaller v3. tbl() reads v1–v4 files; write_vtr() always writes v4.

title: vectra 0.2.2
text: Column pruning: scan nodes read columns needed query plan. Predicate pushdown: filter predicates attached scan nodes use .vtr v3 per-rowgroup min/max statistics skip entire row groups.

title: vectra 0.2.2
text: .vtr format version 3 per-column per-rowgroup statistics (min/max). O(n log n) rank() dense_rank() (replaces O(n²) comparison-based). Nested expressions summarise(): summarise(m = mean(x + y)) auto-inserts hidden mutate.

title: vectra 0.2.2
text: year(), month(), day(), hour(), minute(), second(): date/time component extraction Date POSIXct columns. .Date() .POSIXct() literals filter expressions (e.g. filter(date > .Date("2020-01-01"))). .Date(string_col): convert ISO-format date strings Date values. nchar(): returns string length integer. substr(x, start, stop): substring extraction (1-based, like R). grepl(pattern, x): fixed string matching (regex). paste0(, b): two-argument string concatenation. gsub(pattern, replacement, x) / sub(): fixed-string replacement. startsWith() / endsWith(): string prefix/suffix matching. pmin() / pmax(): element-wise minimum/maximum. log2(), log10(), sign(), trunc(): additional math functions.

title: vectra 0.2.2
text: sd() var(): sample standard deviation variance via Welford’s online algorithm. Returns NA groups fewer 2 values (R semantics). first() last(): first last non-NA value per group. support na.rm = TRUE.

title: vectra 0.2.2
text: slice_min() slice_max() gain working with_ties parameter (default TRUE). Ties boundary now included default; use with_ties = FALSE exactly n rows. count() tally() gain working sort parameter. sort = TRUE returns results descending order count column. transmute() reframe() now support across(). distinct(.keep_all = TRUE) column subset now emits message falling back R.

title: vectra 0.2.2
text: glimpse(): preview column names, types, first values without collecting full result. collect() now works data.frames (-op), slice_min(...) |> collect() works regardless with_ties path.

title: vectra 0.2.2
text: New quickstart vignette: vignette("quickstart"). @details sections added filter(), mutate(), summarise(), arrange(), distinct(), count(), join functions.

title: vectra 0.2.1
text: External merge sort 1 GB memory budget automatic spill--disk. Sort-based group_by() |> summarise() path spill-safe aggregation. Chunked FULL join finalize (65,536 rows per batch). Automatic type coercion (int64 <-> double) join keys bind_rows(). rank() dense_rank() window functions.

title: vectra 0.2.1
text: .vtr format version 2 per-column annotations. Date, POSIXct, factor columns roundtrip write_vtr() / collect(). () predicates work select(), rename(), relocate(), across().

title: vectra 0.2.1
text: Engine reference vignette (vignette("engine")). 17-scenario benchmark suite baseline snapshots regression thresholds. ASAN/UBSAN CI job Linux. Benchmark smoke job PRs.

title: vectra 0.1.0
text: Initial release. Custom columnar -disk format (.vtr) multi-row-group support. dplyr-compatible verbs: filter(), select(), mutate(), transmute(), rename(), relocate(), group_by(), summarise(), count(), tally(), distinct(), reframe(), arrange(), slice_head(), slice_tail(), slice_min(), slice_max(), pull(). Hash joins: left_join(), inner_join(), right_join(), full_join(), semi_join(), anti_join(). bind_rows() bind_cols() combining queries. Window functions: row_number(), lag(), lead(), cumsum(), cummean(), cummin(), cummax(). across() support mutate() summarise(). explain() inspecting execution plan. tidyselect integration column selection helpers. Data sources: .vtr, CSV, SQLite, GeoTIFF. Data sinks: write_csv(), write_sqlite(), write_tiff().
